question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 12 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of a new authentication version caused the increase in latency and request volume.
why_chain: The deployment of auth v5.3 led to increased request volume and latency.
The increased request volume overwhelmed the system, causing autoscaler to scale out.
The scaling out process increased latency due to the load balancing and resource allocation delays.

contributing_factors.description: The flash sale campaign likely caused the spike in request volume and error rate.
why_chain: The flash sale campaign went live, causing a sudden increase in request volume.
The increased request volume overwhelmed the system, leading to higher error rates.
The system's inability to handle the sudden surge in traffic caused the observed latency and error rate spikes.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The autoscaler scaling out was the cause of the increase in latency.
ruled_out.reason: The autoscaler scaling out happened after the change, not before.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The customer support request was the cause of the increase in latency and error rate.
ruled_out.reason: The customer support request happened before the change.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region us-east rose from 137 ms to 295 ms (+116%), with a change point at 2026-03-12T15:10:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region us-east: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for region us-east rose (2792 per 5 min before, 10655 per 5 min after, +282%).
At the same time, error rate for region us-east rose (0.43% before, 0.89% after, +106%).
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in us-east at 15:10 UTC (us-east; 158 min before the change; record R015)
Request volume 3x normal in us-east (us-east; 12 min after the change; record R017)
Deployed auth v5.3 to us-east (auth, us-east; 167 min before the change; record R014)
Customer asks how to download an invoice. (search, us-east; 171 min before the change; record R013)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (us-east; 20 min after the change; record R018)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 167 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✗ Request volume also rose, so a traffic explanation is still open.
✗ 2 other change event(s) fit about as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records from the hour before the change
Details to tell the competing changes apart (e.g. a rollback test)

actions.action: Roll back the deployment of auth v5.3 to mitigate the increased latency and request volume.
Implement traffic management and load balancing to handle sudden spikes in request volume.
Optimize the system's capacity and performance to better handle the expected traffic during campaigns.
